subject: Hosted API rollout: tailed latency spike impacting Storify (urgent escalation)
messages:
From: Alex Gregory <alex.gregory@storify.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 08:57:00 -0700
Subject: [URGENT] p99 spike and error bursts in production since canary rollout

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing a sharp increase in tail latency and a small bump in 5xxs on our Hosted API traffic around 06:45 PT this morning — immediately after Redwood's A/B canary variants were rolled to 10% in our production region. The symptoms:
- p50/p95 roughly unchanged; p99 went from ~280ms to 1.6–2.1s for text generation calls
- occasional 503s when throughput briefly exceeds 120 RPS
- observed dropped throughput on some hosts (saw backpressure logs)

I attached a Grafana snapshot and a short sample trace. This is affecting several customer-facing workflows (user-facing slowdowns). We need escalation and either a rollback or a mitigation asap. Can you confirm you’ve received and what the immediate next step is?

Attachments: storify_grafana_20270625.png (screenshot)

Thanks — we’re on standby.

—Alex

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:22:45 -0700
Subject: Re: [URGENT] p99 spike and error bursts in production since canary rollout — initial findings

Quick summary from SRE triage (initial):
- The canary A variant (v2027.6.24-a) introduced a small change to the KV cache eviction heuristic and a new attention kernel ordering. Under Storify’s token distribution we see an increased rate of KV cache invalidation on long conversations, causing more cache misses and repeated decoding stalls on a subset of hosts. That pattern explains a large p99 delta with little p95 movement.
- Correlated logs: repeated "kv_cache: miss -> fetch" spikes aligning with tail latency windows; per-host 5xx rate rose from 0.02% -> 0.8% when the local queue length > 40.
- Canary traffic: 10% globally; affected instances are a subset (10/120) where the new kernel was selected by the runtime due to sequence length heuristics.

Immediate recommended actions (fast path):
1) Revert canary variant to previous build on affected pool (target: rollback within 30m).
2) If rollback delayed, reduce canary traffic from 10% -> 2% and pin Storify routes to the older variant.
3) Enable temporary per-route concurrency cap (Rlimit=32) for Storify while rollback proceeds.

I’ve attached the collected analysis bundle (canary-analyze-logs-20270625.tar.gz) and a quick mitigation plan. Connor will run the rollback if we get green light. Expected impact: rollback should return p99 near baseline in one to two minutes after drain.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Gregory <alex.gregory@storify.ai>, Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@storify.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:38:05 -0700
Subject: Re: [URGENT] p99 spike and error bursts in production since canary rollout — mitigation plan and timeline

Alex / Sanjay —

Thanks for the quick signal. We are doing the rollback to the previous variant for impacted hosts now. Plan:
- T+0: pause any additional canary promotions across regions (in progress)
- T+10m: reduce canary traffic for Storify to 2% and pin routes -> previous variant
- T+25m: full rollback for affected pool if p99 does not return to baseline after the traffic pin
- Post-incident: 48-hour postmortem with timeline and follow-ups (including a test matrix for long-conversation token distributions)

We will monitor Grafana and share a live dashboard link. If you need an exec walk-through, Laura (COO) and Rishi (Head of Products) are on standby.

Apologies again — we understand the impact and are prioritizing.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
VP, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the rapid response and transparency. We saw an initial improvement after the traffic pin. Two asks while this is being closed out:
1) Please confirm whether Redwood will provide a service credit for the impact window (we logged business impact for ~42 minutes).
2) We’d like an exec-level postmortem and a remediation timeline for preventing rollout-specific regressions that cause tailed latency problems for long-conversation workloads.

We’re available for a 30-min call this afternoon to sync if helpful.

—Alex
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 18:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: [URGENT] p99 spike and error bursts in production since canary rollout — final update and next steps

Alex / Sanjay —

Final update for today: rollback completed for the affected pool at ~10:20 PT; the p99 returned to baseline (~300ms) within ~90s of the rollback completing. We left a reduced canary footprint (2%) for further monitoring and disabled the kernel-change path for long-sequence hosts pending a deeper test.

Action items we committed to:
- Immediate: (done) rollback and reduce canary traffic; monitor for 24 hours.
- 48h: SRE postmortem (owner: Marcus) — includes root-cause, affected host list, and required changes to kernel-selection heuristics.
- 5 business days: Exec postmortem + remediation plan (owner: Laura) — includes a new rollout checklist for tail latency-sensitive customers and required test harness expansions to cover long conversation token distributions.
- Contract: CS will follow up on the credit request and share a proposed credit calculation by EOD tomorrow. (owner: Kimberly)

Attachments: mitigation_plan_20270625.md (short-term steps and monitoring playbook)

We appreciate your patience and will set up the exec-level review per your ask. If you’d like a call tonight, we can do 7pm PT.

Thanks again — we’ll keep this thread updated with postmortem artifacts.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Success (Escalations)
